feeds.title: Early Music Muse Blog
feeds.description: Early Music Muse is intended to appeal to both beginners and specialists in medieval and renaissance music. This blog is written by Ian Pittaway, singer, and player of medieval, renaissance, and early baroque music on period instruments harp, gittern, citole, Symfony, lute, bray harp, cittern, 4-course guitar, mandore, and koboz.

feeds.title: Texas Early Music Project Blog
feeds.description: The Texas Early Music Project preserves & advances Medieval, Renaissance, Baroque, & early Classical music via performance, recordings & educational outreach. Read their blog that shares articles on the latest music news, such as new releases, industry information, interviews, reviews, or discussions about music.

feeds.title: Connecticut Early Music Festival Blog
feeds.description: Founded in 1982 by a group of early music devotees, the New London-based Connecticut Early Music Society presents an annual festival of between six and nine concerts each June. The Connecticut Early Music Festival Blog features articles that explore a particular topic in depth. These features can cover anything from the history of a genre to the latest trends in music technology.

feeds.title: Early Music Review
feeds.description: After more than a decade of printed magazines from King's Music and The Early Music Company, Early Music Review moved online in 2015. The Early Music Review features music reviews, artist profiles, album information, news and updates from music industry.

feeds.title: Early Music Society of the Islands
feeds.description: to The Early Music Society of the Islands!Founded in 1985 and based in Victoria BC, the Early Music Society is a non-profit, volunteer-run society dedicated to offering accomplished performances of music composed prior to 1800. EMSI embraces the idea that early music deserves to be heard close to its original intent. To that end, their concerts feature period instruments, accurate scores, and historical performance practices. Their blog features articles on the music industry, feature stories, instrument knowledge and more.

feeds.title: The Early Music Shop Blog
feeds.description: The Early Music Shop is an independent music shop specializing in Early Music instruments, accessories, and printed music. Their expert staff have years of experience helping you to find the perfect instrument for you! Don't miss the latest news, upcoming offers, and events from the Early Music Shop by following their blog.

feeds.title: Worcestershire Early Music
feeds.description: WEM aims to promote the enjoyment and understanding of music composed before 1800.They promote historically informed performances offering the history and social context of the music performed on authentic instruments. Their audiences enjoy the intimate and sociable atmosphere and the opportunity to ask the performers questions.

feeds.title: Andrew Benson-Wilson : Early Music Reviews +
feeds.description: Andrew Benson-Wilson is an organ recitalist based in England, specializing in early music. In addition to his organ performances, writing has always been an important part of his musical activities. Andrew Benson-Wilson has written several articles on organ and early music topics, as well as a book titled 'The Performance of Early Organ Music'. He also engage in freelance writing and reviewing for specialist early music and organ magazines

feeds.title: Brighton Early Music Festival
feeds.description: Throughout the year, BREMF contributes to the vibrant arts scene in Brighton and Hove through its programme of choral concerts, workshops and schools projects. The annual Festival takes place in late October and early November and has built a reputation for lively and inspired programming, often exploring connections with different art forms and using performance formats and spaces that challenge preconceptions of early music.

feeds.title: Stile Antico
feeds.description: Stile Antico is firmly established as one of the world's most accomplished and innovative vocal ensembles. Working without a conductor, its twelve members have thrilled audiences on four continents with their fresh, vibrant, and moving performances of Renaissance polyphony. Follow the blog and learn more about the music world, latest music performances, feature stories, artist profiles, news and updates.

feeds.title: Elizabeth Eva Leach Blog
feeds.description: Elizabeth Eva Leach is a Professor of Music at the University of Oxford and is both a music theorist and musicologist, with wide-ranging interests in everything from the minutiae of musical structures and manuscripts to the broadest cultural, historical, and philosophical contexts for music. Her principal focus has been on music and poetry of the fourteenth century, although she has also written about songs from both earlier and later periods.

feeds.title: Renaissance Music Academy Blog
feeds.description: Renaissance Music Academy is a renowned music school in Henderson, Nevada, just outside of Las Vegas, Nevada. They are known for offering the most comprehensive lessons for piano, violin, cello, voice, guitar, music theory, music harmony, and music composition in the state. Their instructors are professional musicians with formal conservatory training and an innate passion for welcoming students into the world of music.

feeds.title: West Virginia Renaissance Festival » Music
feeds.description: Visit their blog and learn more about articles, galleries, schedules, and more on music. West Virginia Renaissance Festival Blog is the official website of the West Virginia Renaissance Festival. The festival is presented by the Hanlon-Lees Action Theater and Hollow Hills Farm and is sponsored by Freedom Marketplace. The festival features a variety of activities and entertainment, including bagpipers, a grand joust in honor of King Edward and Queen Eleanor, artisans and merchants selling their wares, savory foods, and local brews, games, music, and dancing.

feeds.title: Early Music Blog
feeds.description: Early Music Blog is in highly informative blog covering various traditional music-related topics and providing useful articles and blogs. The topics covered on the blog are the latest songs, event information, artist profiles, industry news, and updates.

feeds.title: The Early Music Legend Blog
feeds.description: David Munrow did not just emerge into the field of medieval and renaissance music, he exploded into it. He established a standard that can now never be ignored, and the stimulating shock-waves from his explosion will carry far into the future. The Early Music Legend Blog is a tribute blog to a renowned broadcaster and musician. It consists of relevant articles from the internet plus some original, and formerly unpublished material.

feeds.title: The Linarol Consort Blog
feeds.description: The Linarol Consort of Renaissance Viols draws together players who are leading exponents of the viol as both a consort and solo instrument and focuses uniquely on their love of the instrument's very earliest sound and repertoire. Their blog is about music news, such as new releases, tour announcements, and industry information.

feeds.title: Stephen Jones Blog » Early Music
feeds.description: Stephen Jones Blog is a personal blog by Stephen Jones, a British sinologist and ethnomusicologist. The blog is about his research on Daoism in China, particularly the Li family Daoists of Yanggao, Shanxi. Jones's work focuses on the religion of Daoism, and he has written extensively on the Li family's rituals, early music, and language.

feeds.title: Early Music Scores Blog
feeds.description: Felipe Dias is the editor of Early Music Scores and holds a bachelor's degree in Music from Escola de Música da Universidade Federal do Rio Grande do Norte, Natal, RN, Brazil. He is currently pursuing a Master of Music in Early Music Singing at Musikhochschule Trossingen in Germany. His blog editorial focus is mainly on soloistic vocal repertoire, including Italian secular songs, monodies, solo cantatas, English mad songs, French airs de cour, solo motets, and more.

feeds.title: Early Music Seattle Blog
feeds.description: Early Music Seattle is the area's largest presenter of early music and related educational programs. Its mainstage events include Seattle Baroque Orchestra and internationally-renowned touring artists at specific venues. Read the blog that posts articles on music events, artist profiles, interviews, impact on society through music, event information, music reviews and more.
